rationale:
Records a Pulp-owned lifetime fix in the view hot reloader plus the test registration that proves it, and declares the two watch families its file set crosses.

render-assets-and-backends is crossed only through that family's broad core/view/** selector. The change is confined to HotReloader: the destructor now releases the file watcher explicitly before the members its callback writes, and the content-hash compare-and-claim happens under a single lock instead of two. Members are destroyed in reverse declaration order, so the default destructor tore down observed_content_hashes_, pending_mutex_, pending_code_ and has_pending_ while the watcher's background thread was still dispatching into on_file_changed, and the split hash check let the watcher thread and the owning thread both observe the same new content and both report a reload. Nothing under core/canvas or core/render is touched, no renderer, backend, Skia pin, shader, surface, font or asset changes, and no packaging or asset-resolution behaviour changes.

visual-proof-harness is crossed by test/cmake/view_widget_bridge_tests.cmake, which the family names by exact path. The registration is split rather than rewritten: pulp-test-hot-reload is now discovered twice, once for ~[slow] with no label and once for [slow] under a slow:: prefix carrying the slow label, so the millisecond cases keep reaching the required macOS gate and the diff-coverage lane while the file-watcher debounce cases stop starving them. No fixture, snapshot, threshold, harness runner or captured output changes, and no test is removed from any lane it already reached.

Registered watch-only so both families' coverage stays honest about a change that crossed their selectors. No design ingest, captured output, packaging boundary, accepted expansion boundary, or Vellum source authority is affected.
